fields.sample_size: two ongoing NGO-led projects in Delwara (peri-urban Rajasthan, about 7,000 people) and four peripheral wards of Cuttack (Orissa; about 20,000 people); needs assessment and project documentation; no respondent sample or evaluation data
fields.effect_estimate: In Delwara (project started 2004), 50% of households lacked sanitation and as many travelled far for drinking water; community desilting of the Palera pond and repair of feeder channels restored year-round water (no droughts reported in the six years since) and prompted the panchayat to recognise pond maintenance. In Cuttack (started 2009) tube-well water was high in iron; community-built wells, a water filter and women's self-help-group toilets were introduced. The authors conclude community-based water management promotes equity where service-providing agencies fail. Programme description by the implementing NGO; impacts are self-reported and not measured.
fields.study_design: NGO-authored case-study description of two community water-management projects
fields.section: Full text: 4 Community based water management (4.1 Delwara; 4.2 Cuttack); 5 Conclusions

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: an NGO description of two community-based water and sanitation projects (Delwara and Cuttack, India), read in full text 2026-10-04. Reported benefits (perennial pond water, community toilets and filters, panchayat recognition) are self-reported by the implementing organisation; no measured outcomes.
